director.chapterArc: High-adrenaline flight through tactical collapse to paralyzed grief; narrator maintains grounded, analytical distance while filtering chaos through Toren's sensory experience.
director.restraintNote: Avoid 'wonder' tones for magic or heroics. Treat violence as physical maintenance and the Ember's behavior as a biological fact rather than a magical event. The emotional peak is silence after Bram's death; do not swell volume, let phrasing carry the weight.

cues.delivery: Clinical observation of enemy mechanics; flat affect to establish threat logic before panic sets in.
cues.from: At four hundred, the first one came over the guardrail.
cues.through: It didn't jump the rail. It came through the gap where a length of it had rotted out, and it did that poorly, catching a foot and going down on the shoulder gravel and getting up again without any of the pause a person would have taken. That was the first thing Toren understood about them, before he understood anything else: it fell down, and it did not care that it had fallen down.
cues.reason: Establishes the 'husk' as a non-sentient force rather than a monster.

cues.delivery: Sharp, staccato delivery for Bram's action; voice remains flat and utilitarian despite the violence.
cues.through: The sound went up the cut and came back twice. The thing folded at the hips and dropped and did not get up, and Toren had one clean second of relief — oh, they die — and then Bram broke the gun open and thumbed a shell in and said, in the same flat voice he used about weather, "That's a husk. Get behind the cart."
cues.reason: Bram treats death as routine maintenance; no dramatic flair.

cues.delivery: Measured pacing for the magic description; emphasize absence of light/sound through deliberate phrasing.
cues.from: Marta Faust was already down off the cart step with her boots planted and her hands out low and open, and she said a word Toren didn't know, and the air about eight feet in front of her went wrong.
cues.through: Toren had lived eight years in the same settlement as that woman and had never seen her do anything but set bones.
cues.reason: Convey Marta's power as a physical void, not a magical spectacle.

cues.delivery: Accelerated rhythm for Toren's internal panic; shift to fragmented syntax during the attack.
cues.from: He had no memory of taking it out of his pocket. It was just there, cool and flat, and he was running with the cart with his fist closed around it, and behind him something screamed — not a person, a husk, a thin dry sound like a board being pulled off a nail — and he thought, with total clarity: now.
cues.through: He didn't decide anything. His left arm went up because arms do that, and he got it across his own face, and the thing hit him high, and they went down together into the gravel with the whole weight of it on his chest. It smelled like a dry cellar. It had no face, and it was trying very hard to get its arms past his arm, and it was not strong, that was the strange part, it was not much stronger than Wyck, it was only relentless, it had no idea at all that it might stop.
cues.reason: Reflects dissociative state and physical struggle without losing narrator distance.

cues.delivery: Slower cadence for the realization; grounded resonance to emphasize Toren's shift from agency to acceptance.
cues.from: And the Ember in his right fist went hot.
cues.reason: The core thematic turn: the tool decides. Needs weight and clarity.

cues.delivery: Economical delivery for Bram's final actions; brief pause before the description of his death to let the horror land.
cues.from: He set it down on the road, upright against the guardrail, the way you set a tool down when you mean to come back for it. Then he took the hand axe off his belt and walked back past Marta and stood in the gap on the far side of her wall, in the open, in the middle of the road.
cues.through: The wheel came out of the break with a crack and the cart lurched forward and Toren was running again with his hip on fire and his hand out, and he did not look back, because his father had said don't stop for me and it had not been his father who said it and he was already old enough to know the difference and not old enough to bear it.
cues.reason: Bram's sacrifice is utilitarian and silent; avoid melodrama.

cues.delivery: Calm but heavy register for Garrick's dialogue; the 'calm' voice indicates extreme stress and finality.
cues.from: "The Ember." His father's face was grey with dust and there was a cut over his eyebrow and his voice had gone very calm, which was the worst thing about it. "Give it here. Now."
cues.through: Then he let go and turned around and went back three steps and took the brush axe up in both hands, because the cut ahead of them had a bend in it, and around the bend the road was already full.
cues.reason: Garrick accepts failure without panic; his authority is quiet.

cues.delivery: Heavy, dragging pace for the closing image; emphasize physical stillness and sensory overload.
cues.from: Senna sat up in the cart bed, white to the lips, and said clearly, "Put me down and run," and nobody answered her, and Dessa took Pitch's cheek strap in both fists and put her forehead against the mule's neck and started swearing at him steadily and lovingly to keep him from bolting.
cues.through: Toren stood at his father's shoulder with a crooked grey spike sticking out of the bottom of his fist and both ends of the world closing.
cues.reason: Paralyzing grief and shock require a slow-down to convey Toren's inability to move.

pauses.after: It didn't jump the rail. It came through the gap where a length of it had rotted out, and it did that poorly, catching a foot and going down on the shoulder gravel and getting up again without any of the pause a person would have taken. That was the first thing Toren understood about them, before he understood anything else: it fell down, and it did not care that it had fallen down.
pauses.reason: Allow the realization of enemy resilience to land before action resumes.

pauses.after: Not all at once. That was almost worse. They came down in ones and threes, sliding, tumbling, some of them landing wrong and getting up wrong, spilling gravel ahead of them in a long dirty rattle, and there were more coming through the rail gaps at road level, and more further up, and Toren stopped being able to count at somewhere past twenty and started just seeing many, which is what the eye does when the number stops being useful.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; transition from counting chaos to tactical observation.

pauses.after: It fell off him. He lay there. The spike was still out.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the spike's emergence and Toren's survival instinct taking over.

pauses.after: The husks came around Marta's wall on both sides, the way water comes around a stone, and Bram Sark went into them with a hand axe. He was good, he was good — he put down four of them in the first ten seconds with short economical strokes like a man splitting kindling. Then the fifth one got his arm, and the sixth got his leg, and he went down in the middle of the road, and the rest went over him the way they went over the guardrail, without any pause at all.
pauses.reason: Scene break equivalent; Bram is overwhelmed. Silence carries the weight of his death.
Pause for Garrick's realization that he cannot take back control of the Ember.
